newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-TABCORP sees Sky TV resolution soon.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TABCORP sees Sky TV resolution soon.

text.p: Tabcorp Holdings Ltd managing director Ross Wilson said a solution to the standoff with Sky Television, which has blacked out racing telecasts on the company's screens, could be less than 24 hours away.
Speaking to a McIntosh Securities investment conference in New York, Wilson blasted Sky, which holds the racing rights, for demanding a 160 per cent increase in outlet fees.
He indicated that Tabcorp was close to an agreement with racing clubs to help cover the jump in costs.
"We are prepared to pay for part of it of course but not the whole lot.
"I hope that in the next 24 hours or at least by early next week we'll have something resolved."
Wilson said because there was no policy against "discriminatory pricing... we only have one choice - pay someone the money being demanded."
"But given that scenario, it's my view the cost should be shared."
Wilson said he had been discussing the situation with the racing industry since TABCORP screens were blacked out ten days ago by Sky which bought the exclusive rights for telecasts until 2002.
Wilson also told reporters after addressing the annual conference that TABCORP's strong balance sheet could lead to acquisitions in the entertainment and leisure industry.
"We'll look at a few things there but we are not in any hurry. First of all we'll fix up the internals of the company."
The Victorian Racing Club, which runs some of Australia's best-known races, said last week it had offered to pay half of the "exorbitant" fee demanded by Sky.
Sky is owned by Rupert Murdoch's News Corp Ltd and Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
Tabcorp, which buys the Sky service for its betting shops around Victoria, said it could not meet the higher fee as many of the shops would become unviable.
